cells.tense: Something in you has gone quiet and full, and you're not rushing to spend it.
cells.ask: Take one thing you feel and say it to one person in one sentence, then stop there and leave it standing. You'll learn whether the feeling holds without anyone helping it along.
cells.core:
There's a settled read in you that speaks for itself — you take the slower measure of people and situations and it keeps turning out sound, and the easy exchange keeps coming back around because of it. You're at the door of what's arriving and you're reading it accurately, no push needed.

What that steadiness has room for now is going further into a feeling or a thought than the surface before you act — on your own time, following it down. Say the one true sentence out loud and let it stand, and you'll find out how deep the deep end goes.
cells.sheetLine: What you feel has settled, and it isn't waiting on anything.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart already knows before moving on it
cells.place: the point where what's arriving outside reaches the threshold and waits to be let in

cells.tense: You're feeling things forward into outcomes that haven't happened yet, bracing for them early.
cells.ask: Choose one feeling you've been carrying ahead of time and let it finish by itself before you decide anything about it — a day, then one act taken from what's actually here. Ends in ground you didn't have to force.
cells.core:
You can read between yourself and another person, and on a normal day that read steadies both of you with no effort at all. What's happening now is that the feeling runs ahead of the moment: you know how a person will take something before they've opened their mouth, you feel an ending before it starts, and you're living inside a future that's already furnished in your chest. That pre-living is standing where the real contact should be.

So let one of those ahead-of-time feelings ripen on its own schedule before you move on it, and take the next act from what's actually in the room — ending included, if that's the real thing. What waits can be gathered. What's dragged forward can't.
cells.sheetLine: You're feeling the future before it's yours to feel.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart already knows before moving on it

cells.tense: You're still standing at an earlier point, and what's arriving now isn't being let through.
cells.ask: Take the one thought that keeps circling and put it down in a single clear sentence — saying it out loud counts — then say what comes next for you because of it. Ends in a center you can move from.
cells.core:
When this is working, you meet what's coming toward you and rest with it a while before acting — a text that lands and you sit with it, a person across the table and you take in what they actually said, a plan for the week and you know how you feel about it before you move. You read what's already yours, and the act comes from that instead of from the push of the room. Right now what's coming toward you isn't getting read at all. The reception has gone quiet, so what arrives stands outside and doesn't land.

What this needs isn't more feeling — it's pulling your own scattered thinking into one line. One sentence about the thought that keeps spinning, and you'll have somewhere to stand while the rest arrives.
cells.sheetLine: What's arriving now keeps finding you somewhere else.

cells.tense: The steady read of what's arriving is running in you, and you're calling it nothing.
cells.ask: Name out loud one thing you've been sitting with that you'd say is just background noise — say whose it is and where it came from. Ends with you knowing what was already yours.
cells.core:
You can sit with something and know the shape of it without turning it into an argument or a task — you take the day in quietly and the people around you steady because of it. But the sitting gets filed as nothing: you call it zoning out, or being tired, or waiting for something to happen, when it's the same read of the heart doing its work either way. You're inside the depth, describing it as absence.

So take one of those quiet nothings and say aloud that it's yours — name what you've been sitting with. The depth doesn't need to be discovered. It needs to be claimed.
